version.changelog:
cargo-analytics 1.4.2

- Clarified the skill's purpose: analytics is for measuring and exporting data, not diagnosing causes; for explanations and root cause analysis, use the new "cargo-diagnostics" skill.
- Updated the description and main documentation to reference the diagnostics skill for "why"-type questions and error root cause traces.
- Adjusted the scope section with clear guidance and examples on when to use analytics vs diagnostics.
- Removed the legacy skill-card.md file.

llm.summary: This skill is a documented Cargo analytics helper that runs Cargo CLI commands to measure, download, and export workspace data, with no evidence of hidden execution or exfiltration beyond the requested Cargo operations.

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is analytics and data export for Cargo workspaces, and the artifact instructions consistently focus on Cargo CLI metrics, run downloads, batch output downloads, and segment exports.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill includes broad export examples, including full segment exports and email-filtered exports, and one batch rerun example; these are visible and user-directed but can expose or act on business data if used without care.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as the npm package @cargo-ai/cli@latest providing the cargo-ai binary; the skill itself contains markdown instructions only and no executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The required Cargo account authentication and Cargo CLI access are proportionate to querying and exporting Cargo workspace analytics data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Authentication via browser OAuth or API token is disclosed; the artifact does not instruct background agents, startup persistence, local indexing, credential scraping, or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you expect your agent to access Cargo workspace analytics and exports. Treat downloaded runs, segment exports, signed URLs, and email-containing records as sensitive business data, and use Cargo permissions, filters, date ranges, and limits to keep exports authorized and minimal.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The referenced export examples do show broad segment downloads and an email-based filter without privacy-handling cautions, but exporting segment data is an explicit purpose of the skill and the commands are visible, user-initiated Cargo CLI operations rather than hidden collection or exfiltration.
